About 30-ish years ago I remember having a conversation with someone about laptops or just computers in general in relation to the kind of job we did. My observation was that computers don't replaces us, they allow us to be more productive - accomplish more tasks in the same amount of time. They are a tool. And I was making a very poor case suggesting that my company supply me with one. You would have thought I had grown a second head from their reaction. Were they necessary 30 years ago for the kind of job I did? No, but today every single person in a job like that has a laptop, tablet, or uses a smartphone to do their job. They can't do it without one of those devices. And this is true for hundreds, if not thousands of other jobs today. So it didn't replace a person, it made them a more productive person, a flesh and blood robot. Plus with the extra benefit of making our personal lives "better." AI may not make everyone more productive right now, but 10, 20, 30 years from now we'll wonder how we could have ever survived without it being used in some form or fashion in our professional and personal lives.
